thinking_and_logic: The submitted logic scans the array and collects indices where an element equals the target. That differs from the required task of finding two distinct indices whose values sum to the target. The failing tests (basic pair, duplicates, negatives, and two elements) are all consistent with this misread: in those cases, no element equals target, so the function returns an empty list rather than a pair of indices.
code_assessment: Compared to the canonical optimal solution in the answer key (single pass with a hash map of seen values and complement checking), the final code does not attempt pair finding at all and therefore cannot satisfy the spec. The optimal approach would return as soon as it finds complement = target - nums[i] in a dictionary, guaranteeing O(n) time and correct handling of duplicates and negative numbers while preserving original indices. Your code also accumulates potentially many indices, which conflicts with the problem’s guarantee of exactly one valid pair to return.

next_steps.action: Practice the one-pass hash-map complement pattern for Two Sum until you can write it from memory.
next_steps.why: It is the canonical optimal solution here (O(n) time, O(n) space) and directly addresses duplicates/negatives while preserving indices.
next_steps.how: Template: seen = {}; for i,x in enumerate(nums): c = target-x; if c in seen: return [seen[c], i]; seen[x]=i. Then run 3 manual tests: [2,7,11,15],9; [3,3],6; [-1,-2,-3,-4,-5],-8.
